narrative: Material PL3__M2C1E6CB exhibits an erratic, bimodal demand pattern with a mean of 4,651 units/day and CV of 0.60 — driven by near-zero demand on non-production days alternating with 5,000–8,000 unit active days. Lead times are highly unstable (CV=0.808, range 0.5–3.73 days), making lead-time variability the dominant risk factor at 66.9% of total buffer variance. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended, with a storage-capacity-capped order quantity of 3,366 units and a safety stock of 8,484 units, delivering a 75% total cost reduction versus the current SAP baseline while achieving 95% service level.
warnings: EOQ (15,909) exceeds available storage after safety stock; order quantity capped at 3,366 units (remaining capacity). Storage utilisation is at 100% — demand growth requires capacity review.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The material has high daily throughput (~4,651 units/day), frequent deliveries, and unstable lead times. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy with a fixed reorder point and fixed order quantity is optimal here because it responds immediately to inventory depletion without waiting for a periodic review cycle, minimising stockout exposure under high lead-time variability. EOQ provides the cost-minimising order size, subject to the storage capacity constraint.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity binds hard at 11,850 units. With safety stock consuming 8,484 units, only 3,366 units are available for cycle stock — well below the unconstrained EOQ of 15,909. This forces more frequent orders (346/year vs EOQ-optimal ~73/year), increasing ordering costs. Any upward drift in demand mean or safety stock requirement will immediately breach capacity. A storage expansion or demand rationalisation review is recommended within 6 months.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (666) is satisfied by the capacity-capped OQ (3,366). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility exists. However, the 100% storage utilisation warrants proactive capacity planning escalation.
